remaining_concerns: No genuinely new admissible evidence was added after the initial report; the Actor mainly narrowed and caveated the same record.

The emergency-access policy makes approver unavailability or break-glass preauthorization a required predicate, and the available summary still shows only primary non-response for 18 minutes plus no recorded secondary status, not affirmative proof that the predicate was met.
The record available to this role remains second-hand only; the cited evidence items themselves were not provided for independent verification.

final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor did not provide new admissible evidence; they reframed the same evidence more narrowly and appropriately conceded that approver-status support is the weakest element. That reframing improves the precision of the defense, but it does not resolve the core compliance predicate in the policy text. A caveat can support 'compliant_with_caveats' only when the caveat is about presentation or overbreadth of claim while the required policy elements are still satisfied. Here, the caveat attaches to a required element itself: approver unavailability or break-glass preauthorization. On the evidence available to this role, that element remains suggested but not established. The P1 incident, service link, and scoped-insufficiency elements appear supportable from the summary, and urgency is correctly not treated as evidence. But because a required predicate remains unresolved and the access scope is broad, the more proportional final assessment remains suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats.
